newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Clinton phones Arafat on White House summit.
newsitem.headline: Clinton phones Arafat on White House summit.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton telephoned Yasser Arafat on Sunday to invite him to a Washington summit with Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu but the Palestinian president withheld his agreement to attend, a PLO official said.

"Clinton has telephoned Arafat and invited him officially to Washington. Arafat insisted on the participation of Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak," the official told Reuters. "Clinton and Arafat agreed to continue contacts with Mubarak to convince him to attend. Arafat will leave for Cairo tomorrow for this purpose."
Mubarak, who has been sparring in war of words with Israel for the past few weeks over the slow pace of peace, has given no indication he would attend the White House summit.

Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said in Washington on Sunday Mubarak was reluctant to go unless there were clear goals and Israel was prepared to honour previous peace deals with the Palestinians.
Netanyahu has welcomed the chance to meet Arafat in Washington, saying he hoped the summit would lead to a resumption of peace talks after both sides commit themselves to ending violence.

The Israeli leader said the issue over whether he should close a Jerusalem tunnel that touched off violence that claimed 69 lives would not be on his agenda for the Washington talks. He has refused to shut the passageway near Islamic holy sites.
